memory_candidates.content: A regression-anchor fixture that deliberately breaks a production script's logic to prove a characterization case is non-vacuous must apply the mutation to the already-copied sandbox file under test ($SUT), never to the real source-store file ($CORE_DIR or equivalent) -- and must apply it AFTER the sandbox-build step (e.g. setup_sandbox()) that copies the collaborator in, since that step re-copies from the source store and would erase an earlier mutation. This removes both the EXIT-trap fragility (does not fire on SIGKILL/OOM/crash) and the concurrency hazard (a mutated source-store file is observable by any concurrent reader for the whole fixture's duration) in one reorder, with no new harness infrastructure required.

When a mechanical lint must distinguish a real anti-pattern guard from a string literal containing the same text (e.g. a sed replacement string), anchor the regex to the start of the line (after leading whitespace) rather than adding a path exclusion. A path exclusion blinds the detector to a real occurrence of the anti-pattern planted inside the excluded file, which is often exactly where such an anti-pattern's source lives (e.g. in a test fixture). The anchored-start shape separates 'this line IS the guard' from 'this line CONSTRUCTS a string containing the guard's text' without needing to know the file's identity at all.
